_comment: Copy to .claude/settings.json in your template and tune to your stacks. In headless (-p) runs, acceptEdits auto-approves file edits but NOT bash commands — without an allowlist the generator stalls on its first build or test command. In a backend+frontend monorepo this is ONE merged allowlist covering both. Anything not allowed here is auto-denied in headless mode, so the deny list is defense-in-depth, not the only line. Notes: (1) 'cat' is deliberately ABSENT — allowing Bash(cat:*) lets an agent 'cat .env' straight past the Read(.env*) deny; agents have the Read tool. (2) curl is allowed only against localhost WITH THE PORT COLON PINNED: the rule prefix is 'curl http://localhost:' (note trailing colon), so 'localhost.evil.com' cannot prefix-match — and curl accepts flags AFTER the URL, so 'curl -s http://localhost:5173/api -X POST -d ...' works. If your Claude Code version parses these patterns differently they simply never match and curl is denied — fail closed; test one against your version and adjust. (3) Read denies cover nested .env files — a monorepo has backend/.env, not just ./.env. (4) mcp__playwright lets the GENERATOR click through its own UI for self-checks (step 7 of /implement); the evaluator gets it from harness/eval-settings.json. (5) init.sh is the committed environment bootstrap (starts both stacks + smoke test) that /conventions authors and both agents run. (6) Hooks: kill-switch.sh halts ALL tool calls the moment harness/STOP exists (immediate stop, not just between rounds); steer.sh delivers a one-time operator note from harness/STEER.md to the running agent mid-run. The evaluator's evidence-gate hooks live in harness/eval-settings.json. For fully autonomous runs, the safer alternative remains a Docker sandbox with --dangerously-skip-permissions (see README). Pushing, merging, external network fetches, and secret reads stay with the driver/human.
